analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/developer/build.md (head lines 258-267, a new paragraph in the Verify section) and docs/developer/test.md (head hunk at 726-746, a new paragraph about workload tests for the PR reviewer). It touches no provider code, no keys, no attestation or authorization logic, no cache storage code, and no workflow files.

I checked the added text against the threat model for contradictions or weakened guarantees. The text describes CI threat-review routing: Sol/Opus/Sonnet depth selection, integration targeting, a 500-request ceiling, a deadline below the job timeout, and disabled paid manual dispatch and reruns. It also says incomplete final reviews require human review, and that global uncertainty still denies clearance. These statements describe stronger or at least unchanged review controls. They do not alter the trust boundaries TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011, any asset in A-001 through A-017, or the T-041 cache posture.

The reviewed text is documentation, so the actual behavior of the scanner and workflow (for example whether manual dispatch is restricted to unpaid preflight, and whether routing really retains independent depth for AppAttest.swift, Attest.swift and AuthLatest.swift) is not in the supplied evidence and cannot be verified here. If those controls matter, a later pass should read the scanner and workflow sources. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

The test.md base text (units :0 and :2) is truncated at line 485 and the hunk lands around line 726 of the base, so surrounding context was not visible; the patch is complete and contains only added prose. I found no secrets, new endpoints or security-relevant claims in the added text, and no regression.
